patient._comment: 'patient' contains the three sections that may be exposed in the detailed patient display: presentation, answer, and clinical.

presentation._comment: The immutable patient evidence package available for triage. Panel context controls whether other sections are locked or available.
presentation.chiefComplaint: Drunk, fell and cut his head
presentation.quote: I had a few too many and tripped, cut my forehead on the coffee table. It bled a lot. I didn't black out that I know of. Head hurts where I hit it but I feel okay otherwise.
presentation.triageNote: 50-year-old intoxicated male with a forehead laceration from a fall, GCS 15 without reported loss of consciousness, requiring wound repair and sober reassessment to exclude occult head injury.

answer._comment: The authoritative game answer. Explicit ESI, destination, and destination rationale are answer-bearing content; the player's assignment remains session state.
answer.destinationReason: ESI 3 is appropriate because an intoxicated patient with a head strike is expected to need multiple resources for laceration repair and likely head imaging because examination reliability is limited.

clinical._comment: Display-ready clinical interpretation derived from patient.presentation. It preserves clinical meaning but must not explicitly name or identify the correct ESI level or destination; it does not participate in scoring.
clinical.summary: This patient is intoxicated after a fall with a forehead laceration and currently has GCS 15 without reported loss of consciousness.
clinical.acuityReason: Intoxication can conceal evolving head injury and limits immediate clearance; the wound also requires repair and sober reassessment.
expectedResources: Non-contrast head CT when the intoxication prevents reliable clinical clearance
teachingPoints: A normal initial score does not exclude intracranial injury in an intoxicated patient.
Serial examination and a safe discharge plan are necessary even if imaging is reassuring.

possibleClinicalOutcome.disposition: Wound repair, imaging or observation, and serial reassessment would be followed by discharge only when clinically sober and neurologically reassuring.

aiImageGeneration._comment: 'aiImageGeneration' is info for AI to generate the image of the patient. Most images were done with openAI gpt-image-1 using an API, not the app, in July 2026. Look for some python scripts that are used to create these images. Be sure that the anchor-image is available and is provided to the AI - otherwise the images will not be consistent.
aiImageGeneration.pose: seated, holding gauze to his forehead
aiImageGeneration.prompt: Softly-shaded painterly cartoon illustration in a semi-realistic Pixar/Disney style: smooth gradient shading, soft natural lighting, gentle rounded volumes, fine delicate outlines (NOT thick flat cartoon outlines), warm detailed rendering, natural realistic proportions, single character, 3/4 front view, centered, square 1:1. Match the exact painterly style, brushwork, shading, line weight, lighting, and palette of the attached reference image. Subject: a white 50-year-old man, disheveled, seated on a blue padded clinic chair. Pose: holding a gauze pad to his forehead. Expression: bleary and sheepish. Clearly visible: a gauze pad held to the forehead and a disheveled look. No text, no logos.
